title: Sourdough Stuffing
subtitle: Savory and sweet sourdough stuffing is hearty and satisfying. It works perfectly with the rest of your Thanksgiving feast.
intro: While many Southerners claim cornbread dressing as their must-have Thanksgiving side dish, there’s a sizable number of folks who prefer sourdough stuffing.

Powered by tangy sourdough bread, this hearty twist on classic stuffing lends itself to multiple tasty variations, like our Stuffing Muffins and our Veggie-Packed Sourdough Stuffing. If you don’t have day-old sourdough bread, toast fresh bread in the often for about 10 minutes to help it dry out and retain its texture in this recipe.

items: 1 (1 1/2-lb.) day-old sourdough bread loaf, cut into 3/4-inch cubes (about 12 cups)
3/4 cup unsalted butter, divided, plus more for greasing dish
1 medium-size sweet onion, thinly sliced (about 2 1/2 cups)
1/4 cup chopped fresh parsley, plus small leaves for garnish
2 Tbsp. chopped fresh sage, plus small leaves for garnish
1 Tbsp. fresh thyme leaves, plus more for garnish

steps.title: Prepare oven and baking dish
paragraphs: Preheat oven to 375°F. Butter a large (3-quart) baking dish, and set aside. Place bread cubes in a large heatproof bowl.

steps.title: Cook sausage, then onion and celery
paragraphs: Melt 4 tablespoons of the butter in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high. Add sausage; cook, stirring occasionally, until browned and crumbly, about 4 minutes. Transfer to bowl with bread. Place skillet over medium-high heat, and add 4 tablespoons of the butter. Add onion, celery, pepper, and 1/2 teaspoon of the salt; cook, stirring occasionally, until onion is golden brown, about 6 minutes. Stir in parsley, sage, and thyme; cook until fragrant, about 30 seconds.
Transfer to bowl with bread and sausage.

steps.title: Make butter-wine sauce
paragraphs: Add wine to skillet, and increase heat to high. Cook, stirring occasionally, until wine is reduced to about 1/4 cup, about 3 minutes. Add stock and remaining 4 tablespoons butter and 1 teaspoon salt; remove from heat, and stir until butter is melted, about 2 minutes. Pour over bread mixture, stirring to combine. Let cool slightly, about 5 minutes.

steps.title: Add eggs
paragraphs: Gently stir beaten eggs into bread mixture.

steps.title: Bake stuffing
paragraphs: Transfer mixture to prepared baking dish.
Bake, uncovered, in preheated oven until golden brown, about 40 minutes. Remove from oven; garnish with parsley, sage, and thyme. Serve immediately.

blocks.content: Tangy sourdough is the perfect base for this balanced stuffing, with sweet Italian sausage, onion, celery, and a mix of herbs to boost its flavor. To make sourdough stuffing, you'll need:

content.text: A mildly tangy base for the stuffing. The slightly stale texture helps the bread absorb the liquid ingredients without becoming mushy.
Adds richness and enhances the flavor of the sautéed vegetables and herbs.
A savory, slightly sweet sausage that adds heartiness and richness to the stuffing.
Adds a natural sweetness and complexity.
For a subtle crunch and depth.
Enhances the overall flavor.
Fresh herbs to brighten the flavor and add an earthy touch. This trio works especially well together.
An acidic touch to round out the flavors.
Adds moisture to the stuffing for the right consistency.
Binds the stuffing mixture to help set the structure.

blocks.content: To change up this sourdough stuffing based on your preferences or what you have on hand, consider these variations:

content.text: As an alternative, use ciabatta, cornbread, or brioche for a different flavor and texture, adjusting the quantity of liquid as needed for each type.
Swap the sausage with hot Italian sausage, or with turkey or a plant-based sausage for a leaner option.
Swap the onion with shallot or leeks as desired, or add in bell peppers or mushrooms for an added flavor boost.
While we prefer fresh herbs, you can substitute with dried varieties if fresh aren't available, using half the amount.
Substitute with apple cider or omit entirely if needed, adjusting the stuffing with extra stock as needed.
Add toasted pecans or walnuts for added crunch.
Incorporate a sweet touch with dried cranberries or diced apples.
Add in grated Parmesan, Gruyère, or sharp Cheddar for a cheesy addition.
Sprinkle in a pinch of nutmeg, smoked paprika, or cayenne for added warmth.

sections.heading: Our Tips for the Best Sourdough Stuffing

blocks.content: For stuffing with the best texture and flavor, keep these tips in mind:

content.text: Choose an artisan loaf with a chewy crumb and crisp crust for the best texture.
Stale bread is key for the best stuffing—it will absorb the liquid without becoming overly mushy. As an alternative, toast fresh bread cubes before using.
Fresh herbs add color and freshness to the dish.
Avoid overmixing, which could break up the sourdough and result in a mushy stuffing.
Bake the stuffing uncovered for a crisp, golden brown topping and tender center.

sections.heading: Can I Prepare Sourdough Stuffing Ahead?

blocks.content: If you're trying to get ahead of your holiday prep, you can prepare this stuffing ahead as directed, transferring it to the baking dish. Wrap tightly and refrigerate for up to two days. Let stand at room temperature while the oven preheats and bake as directed before serving. If you're afraid of the stuffing becoming too soggy, you can also store the broth and stuffing mixtures separately, then assemble and bake on the day of serving.

sections.heading: How To Store and Reheat Leftover Stuffing

blocks.content: To store and reheat leftover sourdough stuffing, cool completely and wrap tightly or pack into an airtight container. Refrigerate for up to four days or freeze up to three months. You can then thaw large portions overnight in the refrigerator if frozen, or reheat small portions straight from the freezer. Reheat in a preheated 350°F oven, tented with foil to prevent excess browning. Remove the foil in the last few minutes of baking to crisp up the top. You can also reheat the stuffing in the microwave or covered on the stovetop, adding a splash of broth if needed to keep it from drying out.

sections.heading: What To Serve With Sourdough Stuffing

blocks.content: This sourdough stuffing is guaranteed to become a holiday favorite. Pair with classics like roasted turkey or chicken, cranberry sauce, roasted veggies, green beans, mashed potatoes, collard greens, sweet potato casserole, buttermilk biscuits, and more. But you don't have to wait for a holiday to make this recipe. You can also serve it as a hearty side dish to serve with your favorite protein any night of the week.
